charts.annotation: Net flows is disclosed only for some periods (currently H1 FY2026: -£3.0bn); AUM also moves with market performance, so a flat AUM line can still hide negative flows offset by market gains.

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and diluted EPS
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per basic share; diluted EPS additionally assumes conversion of options, awards and other convertible instruments outstanding, so it is always equal to or lower than basic EPS.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): the gap between the two lines is the real-world drag of the employee share schemes the SBC chart tracks -- FY2023's near-zero EPS (0.1p) shows how a thin net income number makes that dilution gap look proportionally large even though the absolute share count barely moved.

What to watch:

  • A widening gap between EPS and diluted EPS (rising dilutive instruments)
  • EPS swings driven by one-offs rather than underlying earnings power

aumFlows.title: AUM and net flows
aumFlows.content:
AUM (assets under management) is the stock of client money Aberdeen is paid a fee on; net flows is the period's new money in less redemptions out -- the flow that AUM's level does not distinguish from market movements.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): this is the headline operating metric for an asset manager -- revenue is a fee rate applied to AUM, so persistent net outflows erode the fee base even while a rising market pushes the AUM bar higher. H1 FY2026 disclosed -£3.0bn of net outflows against AUM of £579.4bn; earlier periods did not disclose the figure, which is why the line is sparse.

What to watch:

  • Net flows turning or staying negative while AUM still rises (market-driven, not flow-driven, growth)
  • Flows relative to AUM (a -£3bn outflow is under 1% of £579bn, i.e. not yet a fee-base crisis)

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Aberdeen Group plc (formerly abrdn plc, formerly Standard Life Aberdeen plc): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
